For even n>=6, each index reflection has exactly two special coordinate orbits whose individual free supports are permitted faces; other reflection orbits are nonadjacent pairs forced to endpoint signs. Because the two special supports are mutually nonadjacent, their parameters vary only on a square boundary; different reflection mirrors can meet only at sign vertices since a nonidentity rotation fixes no positive-dimensional permitted face. Therefore the full mirrored boundary is exactly the labelled reflection-symmetric sign-word graph modulo D_n. Independently generated complete bitmask mirror graphs yielded (mirror vertices,boundary components) n=6:(52,2), 8:(160,4), 10:(424,10), 12:(1036,20); the n=10 component signature is (0,56),(5,40),(9,40),(17,40),(27,40),(51,40),(85,32),(119,40),(165,56),(347,40). Independent face-poset orbit triangulation gives cubical orbit ranks (78,272,136), barycentric f-vector (486,1584,1024), 96 incidence-one edges, Euler -74, and contradictory orientation propagation around an interior dual cycle. A connected nonorientable surface with b=10, chi=-74 has h=2-b-chi=66 crosscaps. Computations exhaust n=10 only; the all-even assertion rests on geometric fixed-locus argument.
